provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The mechanism is a 2x2 block on background palette[0] containing cells of the marker colour palette[2] and cells of another colour C. Each marker cell occupies a corner of the block's bounding box, and that corner gives it a diagonal direction pointing away from the block's centre. In the visible grid, the vertical step is -1 if the cell is on the block's top row and +1 otherwise. The horizontal step is -1 if the cell is in the block's left column and +1 otherwise. A 3-wide colour-C band is drawn from each marker cell as three diagonal rays: one from the cell itself, one from its horizontal neighbour in the band direction, and one from its vertical neighbour in the band direction. Each ray continues until it leaves the grid. The marker cells are recoloured to C and nothing else changes. Because the corner-to-direction rule is defined in visible coordinates, it carries over unchanged under every D4 transform, so the factory only needs to specialise the marker colour (palette[2]) and the background colour (palette[0]). Stopping each ray independently gives the same cells as the constructor's combined loop: each ray moves monotonically and never re-enters the grid once it leaves. Rectangular grids are handled by using separate height and width bounds.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the block colour C differs from the background colour palette[0]; the constructor's random_color is assumed to exclude black. Assumes exactly one 2x2 block with at least one non-marker cell; the constructor uses 1 to 3 directions, so this always holds. If every non-background cell were the marker colour, the program would fall back to C = marker colour. The fixtures fit the uniform rule with no contradictions. No tests have been run.
